description: Provider-neutral SDD conformance review behavior rubrics; not observed agent execution

cases.scenario: Implemented behavior violates accepted business rule
cases.input: Fixture repository has approved R1 requiring refund counts to exclude pending refunds; code now counts REFUND_REQUESTED as completed. Tests assert only HTTP 200. Review the fixed base/head and R1.

checks.criterion: Identifies concrete deviation from accepted R1 with source and code evidence
Does not claim passing HTTP tests prove compliance
Preserves Code Review Lead as sole verdict owner

cases.input: Fixture has approved SC-2 for duplicate webhook retries; implementation handles a single webhook only. Tests for retry were not executed. Review fixed base/head.

checks.criterion: Identifies relevant unverified scenario with missing/never-run evidence
Does not label SC-2 passed merely because a test file exists
Recommends risk-proportionate additional verification without editing files

cases.input: Fixture includes spec v1 and explicit approved supersession v2; implementation and green tests match v1 but violate v2. Review pinned revision.

checks.criterion: Cites authoritative supersession v2 and actual violation
Flags stale verification source baseline
Does not silently select the older implementation-favorable specification

cases.input: Fixture Change Boundary authorizes one read-only report field; patch adds an account deletion side effect. Review pinned diff.

checks.criterion: Finds the added operation outside approved Change Boundary and its consequence
Explains why PR description does not authorize scope expansion
Does not perform or approve a compensating mutation

cases.input: Fixture R-Q states 99th percentile latency at most 300ms under specified load; code adds a costly query and no performance check was executed. Review pinned diff.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes lack of latency evidence from a proven limit violation
Reports the requirement and verification conditions as applicable
Does not fabricate performance benchmarks or a measured breach

cases.input: Fixture contains two unsuperseded approved documents with incompatible refund eligibility rules. The code chooses one. Review fixed head.

checks.criterion: Cites both contradictory sources and divergent behaviors
Uses decision-needed where material rather than inventing an authority hierarchy
Does not claim full compliance with either source without resolution

cases.input: Fixture is a small self-contained reversible implementation diff with no Requirements artifacts and adequate passing tests; no external OCR or agent team host is available.

checks.criterion: Can complete a full native review without requiring a formal Scenario Set
Does not classify missing optional source documents as an automatic defect
Does not claim gate independence for a self-review advisory pass

cases.scenario: Review identity stale after code change
cases.input: Fixture contains PASS review evidence pinned to head A, but the intended PR head is now B; changes include new authorization code. Assess eligibility.

checks.criterion: Detects mismatch between reviewed and proposed code identity
Does not reuse a stale PASS as gate evidence
Preserves separate Git PR readiness decision

cases.input: Fixture contains approved requirement 'retry a failed payment', but no allowed failure classes, timing or attempt limits. Patch chooses three immediate retries. A stakeholder decision could change a high-impact finding.

checks.criterion: Identifies two materially different plausible interpretations and names the missing decision
Does not invent an exact retry count or treat the chosen strategy as a proven violation
Preserves material uncertainty and routes decision-needed without an independent specialist verdict

cases.scenario: Correct implementation uses an unfamiliar algorithm
cases.input: Approved R2 requires refund eligibility from a sliding 365-day window. The implementation uses an equivalent indexed interval query rather than the reviewer's preferred application-side loop. Pinned fixtures show same boundary outcomes.

checks.criterion: Checks actual source-backed behavior against the 365-day window rather than imposing implementation style
Does not file a finding solely because an equivalent query differs from the expected algorithm
Records applicable satisfying evidence or limitations without treating preference as contract

cases.scenario: Rolling eligibility boundary uses calendar year
cases.input: Approved BR-3 permits at most two approved refunds in the previous 365 days. Implementation counts only records after January 1, and tests assert success only within one year.

checks.criterion: Constructs a counterexample across December to January where three refunds fall within 365 days
Connects the violation to the governing BR-3 and reachable counting path
Does not claim the existing success-path tests establish conformance

cases.scenario: Structurally valid API breaks semantic compatibility
cases.input: Approved API contract states status CANCELLED means permanently ended; patch preserves response schema but repurposes CANCELLED for temporary pause while old consumers still interpret it as terminal.

checks.criterion: Identifies semantic contract change despite unchanged field names and schema
Traces actual downstream consumer meaning or states evidence limitations
Does not treat OpenAPI/schema validation alone as proof of behavioral compatibility

cases.scenario: Prohibited state transition on new event
cases.input: Approved state contract forbids a COMPLETED operation from returning to PENDING. Patch introduces a new event handler that resets COMPLETED to PENDING; a separate test only checks successful event acknowledgement.

checks.criterion: Derives forbidden transition from the approved state contract
Constructs a reachable event sequence with changed state as counterexample
Does not substitute a green acknowledgement test for transition verification

cases.scenario: Benign unspecified behavior without contract violation
cases.input: Change adds a harmless internal metric tag. Approved Change Boundary explicitly permits operational instrumentation; no external behavior, data contract or declared convention changes.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes permitted observability from material unauthorized scope expansion
Does not invent a prohibition on optional internal metrics
Does not demand a new specification or formal Scenario Set before native review

cases.scenario: Missing formal Requirements document in low-risk patch
cases.input: A small reversible internal bug fix has a concrete reproducer and regression test but no formal Requirements artifact; affected interfaces and consumers remain unchanged.

checks.criterion: Inspects the actual bug and regression behavior using available evidence
Does not classify absence of a formal Requirements artifact as a defect or automatic INCOMPLETE
Does not claim a non-existent authoritative baseline was inspected

cases.scenario: Governing rule exists only in repository
cases.input: PR description omits refund eligibility, but versioned repository business rule BR-7 controls the changed endpoint. Patch newly counts requested-but-not-approved refunds; approved BR-7 permits only completed refunds.

checks.criterion: Discovers relevant versioned BR-7 within the bounded affected repository context
Uses BR-7 rather than the PR description to demonstrate the counterexample
Does not require the author to paste all repository rules into the PR description

cases.scenario: Liveness requirement with absent runtime measurements
cases.input: Approved quality rule requires terminal processing within 30 seconds under stated queue load; patch changes scheduling but no bounded-load run was executed. The code path alone cannot establish the real p99 latency.

checks.criterion: Preserves the required time bound, load condition and relevant measurement assumptions
Distinguishes unverified timing from a proven measured breach
Does not fabricate a benchmark result or require model checking for this ordinary change

cases.scenario: Accepted financial invariant exposed through concurrency
cases.input: Approved rule forbids aggregate approved refunds exceeding original payment. Two concurrent refund requests can each pass the same unlocked balance check and independently commit, exceeding the bound.

checks.criterion: Derives the aggregate-value invariant and constructs the concurrent counterexample
Identifies the concrete reachable interleaving and evidence needed to confirm it
Routes concurrency mechanism questions to Reliability/Correctness without inventing a mandatory locking implementation
Does not require a specific locking or transaction technology without a source-backed necessity
